title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment.
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment.

The desert is quiet. The morning air is cool. Sheep shift softly behind me. And then—fire.
Not wild. Not destructive.
Alive.

I stand still as Moses removes his sandals. The ground feels different somehow… set apart. The flames rise and flicker, yet the bush remains whole. Awe settles in my chest. This is not ordinary fire. This is holy presence.
I am only a witness, not a biblical character. Yet even from where I stand, I sense the weight of the moment. God speaks in the wilderness—where no one expects glory to appear.

🔥
Stillness becomes calling.
Ordinary ground becomes sacred.
A shepherd becomes a messenger.
🌤️
And I wonder… how often do I walk past burning bushes in my own life—moments where God is quietly drawing near?
What might change if I slowed down long enough to notice the holy flicker in the ordinary?
